answer: Each identity posts a bond before its first claim, and the bond stays locked for 12 epochs after its last graded submission. A replay is the cheap attack, so the node stores a hash of every accepted kernel per epoch and compares on arrival; a duplicate revokes the bond and the payout it backed. Assume the attacker read the rule first: 12 epochs of dead capital per key is the entry fee. An orchard of 400 keys at 250 POA each locks 100,000 POA before earning a point, while one honest falcon locks 250, and one duplicate anywhere costs the bond.
